reason: While the passage names Abram (who is established as a patriarch and leader) and God (YHWH), it also names Sarai (אִשְׁתּוֹ - his wife) and Lot (בֶן־ אָחִ֗יו - his brother's son). Sarai is presented as Abram's wife who follows him, and Lot is depicted as following Abram (וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ לוֹט - Lot went with him). Neither Sarai nor Lot are depicted in leadership positions within this passage; they are followers and dependents, not leaders.
